structured_output.scope_summary: EIP-7979 adds three EVM instructions: CALLSUB (pop a destination, push PC+1 to a new return stack, jump), CALLDEST (a no-op subroutine-entry label costing 1 gas), and RETURNSUB (pop the return stack into the PC). The return stack is a new part of machine state that EVM code cannot read or write directly. It holds at most 1024 entries, and both overflow and underflow cause an exceptional halt. Jump-destination analysis is extended so CALLDEST is a valid target for CALLSUB, JUMP and JUMPI, which changes the set of valid destinations for the existing jump instructions. Opcode byte values are still to be decided. EIP-8173 is an informational background document and defines no protocol rules.

evidence.summary: The new opcodes use the existing constant tiers: mid (8), jumpdest (1) and low (5).

evidence.locator: Reference Implementation - "GAS_MID (8), GAS_LOW (5), and GAS_JUMPDEST (1) are EELS's existing constants"
evidence.summary: No new gas-accounting mechanism is added and no existing gas rule changes.

evm_gas_rule_changes.rationale: The only gas items are constant costs for new instructions, using existing tiers. No metering, limit or settlement rule changes, and no existing operation's gas result changes. Testing these costs belongs under added opcodes.
evm_gas_rule_changes.uncertainty_note: The EIP notes that benchmarking may change the costs, but these would still be constant per-opcode costs.

The instruction × destination-type table is small and can be enumerated, so it is not treated as an elevated matrix.
